title: How Can Video Generative AI Transform K-12 Education? Examining Teachers’ Perspectives through TPACK and TAM
extended_summary:
This paper examines how K-12 teachers perceive the educational potential and limitations of video generative AI (Video GenAI), an emerging form of AI that can create video from natural-language prompts. The study is framed by TPACK and TAM, and asks what teachers’ first impressions are, what educational uses they envision, and what barriers they anticipate for classroom adoption.

The researchers conducted online semi-structured interviews with 10 purposively selected participants: eight elementary school teachers, one high school English teacher, and one former elementary teacher who worked as a data analyst. Participants were given access to Luma Dream Machine and an instructional guide so they could experiment with the tool before discussing it. The context was K-12 education in South Korea, and the study focused on teachers with comparatively strong interest in and experience with educational technology and AI.

Findings suggest that teachers saw Video GenAI as promising for visualizing abstract content, supporting creative expression, enriching project-based learning, and enabling new forms of formative and summative assessment. At the same time, they raised substantial concerns about technical quality, language support, hallucinations, safety, copyright, age restrictions, infrastructure, and the lack of institutional guidance. The paper concludes that Video GenAI could be pedagogically valuable, but only if technical, ethical, and policy barriers are addressed and teachers receive appropriate professional development and support.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI video creation tool for producing dynamic, customized visual content from natural language prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Teachers were given access to Luma Dream Machine, a video generation AI platform, and an educational guide so they could experiment with video generation and discuss its K-12 instructional applications in interviews.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study of ten selected teachers’ perceptions and hands-on impressions, not an experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation of outcomes. It does not measure teacher-practice change or student outcomes, so causal evidence strength is low.
impact_tier_rationale: No effect sizes or outcome impacts are reported, and the paper focuses on perceived potential, barriers, and intended use rather than demonstrated impact. The evidence does not establish measurable benefit on instruction or learning.
